use_case_summary: Cadence Stormworks runs a multi-tenant contact-center platform for mid-market retailers. Primary focus: keep agent-assist and async ticket summarization responsive during heavy user spikes (Black Friday / holiday returns). Also want safe tool-calling (CRM writes) with idempotency guarantees under retries and clear audit trails.
spike_reliability_requirements: 99th-percentile latency target: <350ms for agent-assist (turn-by-turn) during 2x baseline QPS
throughput target: sustain bursts up to 4x baseline for 10-30 minutes without request failures
graceful backlog: prefer queued requests with progressive fallbacks (lower-cost model variant or cached replies) instead of hard failures
prefetch / prewarm: ability to pre-allocate KV cache and model warm instances ahead of predictable peaks
transactional tool-calls: end-to-end at-least-once semantics + audit ID for CRM writes
observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and spike alerts tied to runbook links
technical_notes: Current infra: multi-region GCP + hybrid VMware in US-east for customers requiring on-prem components
Traffic profile: conversational chat (median 7 tokens per turn), high frequency api calls from agents during peak campaigns
Preferred models: 1-2 open variants; willing to use quantized variants if latency and determinism preserved
Desired routing: route to cheapest compatible variant unless latency SLO breached, then fallback to dedicated hot lane
Batching tolerance: agent-assist requires sub-200ms tail when possible — so batching windows must be adaptive
Caching: heavy prefix reuse across agents — prefix/KV caching recommended to cut per-token cost during spikes
poC_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): baseline measurements on Hosted API with synthetic spike harness; collect 50th/95th/99th latency and token costs
Phase 2 (48hr): Dedicated pool with prewarm script, cache warm-up, canary traffic (5% of live) and controlled 4x bursts; validate autoscaling thresholds and backpressure policy
Phase 3 (1 week): tool-calling durability tests (simulated CRM writes) with chaos injected: network latency, instance preemption, duplicate requests
Success criteria: no more than 2% request failure during bursts, 99th latency under target, and reproducible cost telemetry
notes: AE notes: company highly cost-sensitive but prioritizes availability for paid enterprise customers — wants clear levers to trade cost vs tail latency

Legal: need 90-day data residency mapping and KMS envelope flow for audit logs
